root_cause.text: Off-by-one error in the bounds check of `hvc_iucv_get_private()` where `num > hvc_iucv_devices` allows index `num` equal to `hvc_iucv_devices`, leading to an out-of-bounds read of the `hvc_iucv_table` array when `hvc_iucv_devices` equals `MAX_HVC_IUCV_LINES` (8).
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the condition from `if (num > hvc_iucv_devices)` to `if (num >= hvc_iucv_devices)`. The commit message explicitly states: "If hvc_iucv_devices == 8, (a) allows the code to access hvc_iucv_table[8]. Oops." and the CVE description describes this as an off-by-one in the number of supported devices.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix off-by-one boundary check in hvc_iucv_get_private to prevent out-of-bounds array access when num equals hvc_iucv_devices.
intent_record.what: Changed the condition from 'num > hvc_iucv_devices' to 'num >= hvc_iucv_devices' in the hvc_iucv_get_private function.
intent_record.how: Previously, when num equaled hvc_iucv_devices, the condition was false and the function would access an out-of-bounds array element. Now, the condition correctly rejects indices equal to the array size, returning NULL for invalid indices.
